FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5

Our Earth & space — the parent shelf: 24 cards to download and print.

The whole sky deck for printing at home: twenty-four Earth-and-space cards for ages four to five, each with its parent tip, its three pills — age, subject, level — its download button and one-tap printing; the library is the parents’ side of the class, so everything happens on this one shelf.

This is the parents’ copy of Class 43 · Our Earth & Space: all twenty-four sky cards on one shelf, ready to print. You do not need a plan — pick the question tonight is already asking, download the card, and print it full size on A4 or Letter paper. Every card carries one parent tip underneath and four pills on top: the age it suits, the subject it teaches, the grade level to start at, and the skill it builds. The download button takes the full-size card; the print button runs a single card through your printer with nothing else on the page. There are no card pages to hop through: the shelf is the whole set.

The shelf is yours; the lesson is your child’s. The class page at Our Earth & Space teaches each idea the way a teacher would — the sky idea said kid-first, one thing to try out the window — while this wall simply holds the deck for printing. Same twenty-four cards, two jobs: the lesson lives in the class, the library is where parents print.

THE THREE LEVELS

Preschool, Grade 1, Grade 2.

Every card wears a level pill so tonight’s card takes one glance to choose. The levels are a suggested order, not a test — the question your child just asked is always the right card.

  1. 01

    Preschool · Name it

    the eight cards to start with — sun, moon and Earth, the ocean and the mountain, day and night, sunrise and sunset, and the weather words a four-year-old hears every single day.

  2. 02

    Grade 1 · Do it

    the nine doing cards — the planet names, rocks and fossils, recycling, sun power, and the rockets, rovers and space suits that turn pretend play into a mission.

  3. 03

    Grade 2 · Own it

    the seven bigger ideas — the spinning Earth, eclipses and tides, the equator and the poles, climate zones, and the far-space finish from comets to black holes.

MY BLUE PLANET SHELF · 4 CARDS

My blue planet — the ground, the water, the air.

Printable Earth flashcards for kids: landforms, rivers and forests, rocks and fossils, and taking care of the water and air — the planet science that starts in your own backyard. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE SUN’S FAMILY SHELF · 5 CARDS

The sun’s family — meet the planets.

Solar system flashcards for preschool and up: our sun and moon, the rocky planets, the four giant planets, dwarf planets and the ringed planet — planet names kids love to shout. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE SPINNING DAY SHELF · 4 CARDS

The spinning day — why the sun comes up.

Day and night, sunrise and sunset, the seasons and the spin of Earth — the sky science kids ask about at bedtime, with a job to try out the window. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE WEATHER & WORLD SHELF · 4 CARDS

The weather & world shelf — what the sky is doing.

Weather flashcards plus the whole-planet map: wind, thunder and lightning, sun power and wind power, the equator and the poles, and the three climate zones — weather words for the morning routine. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE ROCKETS & ASTRONAUTS SHELF · 4 CARDS

The rockets & astronauts shelf — blastoff!

Space travel flashcards: rockets, astronauts and space suits, rovers and landers, satellites and space stations, space walks and moon bases — pretend-play fuel for future astronauts. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.

THE STARS & FAR SPACE SHELF · 3 CARDS

The stars & far space shelf — very big ideas.

Star flashcards and the deep-space finish: stars and galaxies, comets, asteroids and meteors, constellations and black holes — the big words said small enough for a five-year-old. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer.
